title: FizzBuzz
description: Given a number n, return an array of strings for numbers 1 through n: "FizzBuzz" if divisible by both 3 and 5, "Fizz" if divisible by 3, "Buzz" if divisible by 5, or the number as a string otherwise.
whatShouldHappen: Loop from 1 to n inclusive.
Check divisibility by 15 first (both 3 and 5), then 3, then 5.
Push the appropriate string into the result array.
Return the result array.
patternExplanation: Order matters: check the most specific condition (divisible by 15) before the general ones (divisible by 3 or 5) — otherwise the specific case is silently absorbed by an earlier branch.

title: Move Zeros to End
description: Given an array of integers, move all zeros to the end while preserving the relative order of non-zero elements. Modify the array in-place.
whatShouldHappen: Use a write pointer starting at 0.
Loop through the array with a read pointer.
When the read pointer finds a non-zero, write it at the write pointer and advance both.
After the loop, fill the remaining positions from the write pointer to the end with zeros.
patternExplanation: A write pointer only advances when a valid element is found — this compacts all valid elements to the front in one pass, then fills the tail separately.

title: Spiral Matrix Traversal
description: Given an m x n matrix, return all elements of the matrix in spiral order using boundary pointers (top, bottom, left, right).
whatShouldHappen: Define 4 boundaries: top = 0, bottom = m - 1, left = 0, right = n - 1.
Traverse right along top boundary, then increment top.
Traverse down along right boundary, then decrement right.
If top <= bottom, traverse left along bottom boundary, then decrement bottom.
If left <= right, traverse up along left boundary, then increment left.
Continue while top <= bottom and left <= right.
patternExplanation: Contracting 4 boundary variables after each perimeter cycle ensures every cell is visited exactly once in clockwise spiral order.

title: Rotate Array by K Steps In-Place
description: Given an integer array nums, rotate the array to the right by k steps in-place using the three-reversal trick with O(1) extra space.
whatShouldHappen: Normalize k = k % nums.length.
Reverse the entire array from 0 to n - 1.
Reverse the first k elements from 0 to k - 1.
Reverse the remaining elements from k to n - 1.
Return the rotated nums array.
patternExplanation: Reversing the entire array followed by reversing both individual halves accomplishes full cyclical rotation in O(n) time and O(1) memory.

title: Next Greater Element
description: Given an array of numbers, for each element find the first greater element to its right. If no greater element exists, set it to -1.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize result array filled with -1.
Maintain a monotonic decreasing stack of indices.
Iterate through array with index i: while stack is not empty and nums[stack.top] < nums[i], pop top and set result[top] = nums[i].
Push current index i onto stack.
Return result.
patternExplanation: A monotonic stack stores indices of elements waiting for a larger value. Each element is pushed and popped at most once in O(n) total time.

title: Find First Missing Positive
description: Given an unsorted integer array nums, return the smallest positive integer that is not present in nums in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space using cyclic placement.
whatShouldHappen: Use cyclic sort: place each number x where 1 <= x <= n at index x - 1.
Iterate i from 0 to n - 1: while nums[i] is in [1, n] and nums[nums[i]-1] !== nums[i], swap nums[i] with nums[nums[i]-1].
After placement, scan the array: the first index where nums[i] !== i + 1 corresponds to missing number i + 1.
If all indices match, return n + 1.
patternExplanation: Using array indices as a direct hash table allows mapping values to indices in O(n) time while maintaining O(1) auxiliary space.
